dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.utterance: Good morning doctor. I have been having this terrible worsening cough and low-grade fever for three weeks now.

dialogue.speaker: Physician
dialogue.utterance: Good morning. Three weeks is persistent. Are you experiencing any shortness of breath, difficulty breathing, or pleuritic chest pain?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.utterance: No chest pain at all, and no real shortness of breath when resting, but I feel moderately fatigued and achy.

dialogue.speaker: Physician
dialogue.utterance: Have you noticed any phlegm color or blood when coughing?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.utterance: A little bit of yellowish phlegm in the mornings, but definitely no blood.

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.utterance: By the way, my neighbor was telling me about a television series she watched last night, it was really interesting.

dialogue.speaker: Physician
dialogue.utterance: Let us stay focused on your health for a moment. Do you have any known medical allergies, particularly to antibiotics?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.utterance: Yes, I am severely allergic to penicillin. I got hives and swelling the last time I took amoxicillin as a teenager.

dialogue.speaker: Physician
dialogue.utterance: Thank you, that is crucial information. Any history of asthma, COPD, or smoking?

dialogue.speaker: Patient
dialogue.utterance: No, never smoked, and no chronic lung conditions.
